title: Etale source transport preserves universality of constant arrows
statement:
theorem etaleNormalizationArrow_universal_of_constant
    (Y : Scheme.{t}) {R S : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (q : R →+* S)
    {E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t + 1} R)}
    {E' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t + 1} S)}
    (d : E ⟶ (normalizationModuleRestrict q).obj E')
    (h : Nonempty (StructuredArrow.IsUniversal (StructuredArrow.mk d)))
    (U : Y.Etale) :
    Nonempty (StructuredArrow.IsUniversal (StructuredArrow.mk
      (etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow Y q
        (normalizationConstantArrow Y.smallEtaleTopology q d) U)))

source.place: Tags 06YY and 03ED, scalar extension and inverse image on an etale source

proof.text: On any site J, form the natural isomorphism from the constant sheaf on J.over U to the restriction of the constant sheaf on J. Prove its naturality using the constant-sheaf adjunction. Its compatibility with restriction of coefficients follows by applying that adjunction and the sheafification-unit identities for constantCommuteCompose and constantSheafOverHom. These are elementary calculations with the existing sheafification maps.

Derive this exact comparison and use composition of exact derived squares to identify its coefficient square with sliceRestrictScalarsIso. Naturality then identifies the transported normalizationConstantArrow with the constant normalization arrow on the slice.

Apply normalizationConstantArrow_isUniversal on the slice site. Transport its initial structured arrow through the source constant-comparison isomorphism, using StructuredArrow.map₂ and StructuredArrow.isoMk. This proves universality of the restricted constant arrow with its canonical slice coefficient comparison.

Transport the resulting initial object through the derived etale slice equivalences, using their coefficient comparison. The existing etale_source_slice_normalization identity identifies the transported arrow with etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow after the source and target restriction isomorphisms. Initial objects are preserved by these equivalences and isomorphisms.
